sections.heading: A few things you may be wondering.

items.a: AgentsPilot is designed for independent professionals and small service businesses that want help organizing the day and managing the work around their clients.

items.q: Do I need to understand AI?
items.a: Start by describing your business and what you need help with. AgentsPilot helps you shape the workspace and review the next steps in everyday language.

items.q: What if I already have tools I like?
items.a: Start with the capabilities you need. Where a supported connection is available, you can bring activity from an existing tool into AgentsPilot. Check the available connections before relying on a particular workflow.

items.q: Will it contact clients without asking me?
items.a: You choose which activities to authorize and when approval is required. Review the settings for each workflow before enabling it. You can pause an enabled workflow when you need to.

items.q: Does it run my whole business for me?
items.a: You stay responsible for business decisions. AgentsPilot helps organize the work, highlights what needs attention, and carries out the routine activities you authorize.

items.q: What does “learns how I work” mean?
items.a: It means using the business information, preferences, and activity available in your workspace to make its suggestions more relevant. It does not mean it knows everything happening in your business.

corrections.claim: Replies are drafted for the owner to review and approve before sending.
corrections.finding: Not how it works. `reply_to_enquiries` is keyed on `lead_autosend_enabled`; the reply is queued `status: 'pending'` and sent by a drain after 15 minutes. `pending` means awaiting SEND, not awaiting approval — LeadResponseRepository says so explicitly. The 15 minutes is the owner's window to change or cancel (`cancelPending`, skip_reason `cancelled_by_owner`).
corrections.note: The approved fallback copy also claimed review-and-approve, so switching the autonomy gate off would not have made the page true. Both paths were rewritten.

corrections.claim: Follow-ups stop if the person replies, books, or opts out.
corrections.finding: Only the booking case was found. No reply detection and no `email_unsubscribes` check in the lead-response path. The other two stops were removed rather than softened.

It does not write anything. `queueLeadReply` resolves a booking URL and `buildLeadReplyCandidates` builds a fixed invitation listing the business's services, each with a booking link. Nothing is composed per enquiry. It also returns EMPTY with no bookable link — `if (!input.bookingUrl) return candidates` — so a business with no booking page sends nothing at all, and LeadAlertService logs 'No auto-reply queued: this business has no bookable link yet'.
corrections.note: This correction replaces an earlier one from the same day that had already rewritten the step. The first pass fixed the approval claim and left 'writes the reply' standing.

corrections.claim: The day demo showed one flow: an inquiry, a suggestion, a reply.
corrections.finding: Accurate but tiny. It described a single automation and missed the day. The platform sends a narrated MORNING BRIEF (BriefingFactsService: today's appointments, who has not returned intake, who has not paid, what money landed, cancellations and no-shows) delivered by email and as a dashboard card, and runs SIX unattended automations — remind_about_meeting, chase_intake, chase_invoices, chase_quotes, reply_to_enquiries, auto_complete_meetings — each with its own switch.
corrections.note: Rewritten as a real day: the brief before you start, the chasing that happens without you, and the one thing kept back for a person.
